text:
sam: Hey, trying to follow a trace -> find all raw request log lines for request_id=7f9c2b... Console only shows trace_id=tr_01F8XYZ. Fastest path to raw logs? console vs CLI?

 tasha: If you have the request_id, Console -> Observability -> Requests, paste the id in the search bar. Click the request, then "Show raw events" to expand the log lines. :mag_right:

 sam: I only have trace_id from an APM link, no req id. Can I derive req ids from the trace?

 ryan: Yep. CLI is easiest: `rwd trace export --id tr_01F8XYZ | jq -r '.spans[].meta.request_id' | sort -u` will dump any attached request_ids. Then `rwd logs fetch --request-id <id>` or `rwd logs tail --request-id <id> --since 1h`.

 ben: If you don't have the CLI, Console -> Traces -> open the trace -> bottom pane "Related requests" lists req ids with links to the Request view.

 infra-bot: heads-up: high-throughput routes are sampled. If the trace isn't in the index, try `rwd traces search --approx-start 2026-03-15T10:00:00Z --tag span.name=generate` to widen the search window.

 tasha: Also helpful: exported spans include host/pod tags. You can `kubectl logs -n inference -l app=runtime -c runtime --since=30m | rg 7f9c2b` to grep pod logs directly (use a tight time window).

 ryan: One gotcha: `rwd trace export` sometimes nests request_id under different keys. Try `rwd trace export --id tr_01F8XYZ | jq -r '.spans[] | .meta.request_id // .meta["event.request_id"] // .tags[]? | select(.)'` to catch variants.

 sam: Any retention/permission caveats? UI shows truncated ids so I worry about missing full ids.

 tasha: UI truncates for display but the full id is in the trace export and the request detail copy button. For older data we archive raw requests to S3 under `requests/YYYY/MM/DD/<full_request_id>.log` — you'll need infra read access to that bucket.

 ben: If you still can't find lines, try `rwd logs fetch --trace-id tr_01F8XYZ --format json | jq -r '.[].line' | rg 7f9c2b` — some ingestion paths attach trace_id to log entries.

 sam: Trying now, will report back.

 sam: Update: `rwd trace export` returned two request_ids: `7f9c2b1a` and `7f9c2b1b`. `rwd logs tail --request-id 7f9c2b1a --since 2h` found the raw lines. Thanks :tada:

 ryan: Nice. I'll add a short recipe to DevEx with these CLI steps.

 devex: thanks — will link it from Console help and the Observability runbook.
